headline: After a mild Saturday, very strong winds arrive Sunday and a storm brings Sierra rain and snow Sunday afternoon into Monday, including around Mammoth Lakes, with another, less certain storm possible Tuesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday runs 5 to 10 degrees warmer than normal, with Sierra communities such as Mammoth Lakes in the upper 40s to low 50s and many valley locations in the mid to upper 50s. Winds stay light in the valleys, and Sierra ridge gusts of 40 to 50 mph ease through the morning. Southwest winds start picking up again late Saturday night.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Sunday turns very windy: Sierra ridge gusts reach 70 to 80 mph by morning and top 95 mph later in the day, Sierra valley gusts reach up to 50 mph, and Nevada valley gusts reach 30 to 40 mph, with wind-prone spots in Mono County up to 50 mph. Rain and snow reach the Sierra around midday Sunday, with a 70 to 90 percent chance in Mono County, 90 percent in the northern Sierra and northeast California, 50 to 70 percent along the Reno–Carson City area, and under 10 percent in Churchill and Mineral counties, plus about a 15 percent chance of lightning in the Sierra Sunday afternoon. Snow levels start high at 8,000 to 8,500 feet and fall to 7,000 to 7,500 feet for the Tahoe Basin and southern Sierra (as low as 6,500 feet in northeast California) by early Monday; the heaviest precipitation ends Monday morning with lingering Sierra showers Monday afternoon, and snow totals through Monday night stay light at 2 to 6 inches along the Sierra crest and up to 9 inches on the highest peaks.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another storm is possible Tuesday into early Wednesday, but confidence is low because the computer models are struggling with how the incoming low pressure system splits as it moves inland. Recent model runs have shifted the storm farther south, leaving the Sierra on its northern edge, and expected snow amounts have been trending down for the past couple of days. A break in the storms is likely Wednesday through Friday, with more storms possible next weekend.

watch_for: Sierra ridge gusts over 95 mph Sunday and Lake Wind Advisories from Sunday morning into Monday morning
Falling snow levels and slick mountain roads Sunday night into Monday
The track of Tuesday's storm, which has been trending south and lighter
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the mild Saturday and the windy, wet Sunday–Monday storm, but confidence is low for Tuesday's storm; a dry break Wednesday through Friday looks likely.
